claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged on this RydeX trip is a fee the rider disputes as wrongful, and the question is whether it survives NS-1 on the system records.

The rider is the cancelling party and cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance, i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, which is the branch NS-0 sends to NS-4

The rider's own message at 09:05 said only "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" (F10), while the driver had already announced his arrival at 09:03 (F9); the chat is fully timestamped and does not retract the fee or show any agreement by the driver to waive the waiting requirement.

The only remaining statutory escape in NS-4 would be a rule that a driver arriving late frees the rider to cancel free of charge, but Ryde publishes no such rule (NS-8 is informational only and is not cited); F5 shows the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40, only 2 min 30 s after acceptance, so no such argument is available on these facts.

weaknesses: The strongest rider-side point is that the driver himself waited longer than the policy requires and the rider was visibly on the way: F10 ("Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" at 09:05) shows the rider was actively complying and not absconding, which a human reviewer could read as a reason for a discretionary waiver under NS-7; but NS-1 is satisfied on F1/F2/F3/F6, so NS-7's 30-day voucher review is the rider's only route, not a Rules-based win.

events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F4], so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4 for an on-demand booking [F4][RD-NS-0]. The system records settle the key timings: acceptance at 09:00:10 and rider cancellation at 09:09:10, i.e. 9 min 0 s after matching [F4], well past the 3-minute free-cancellation window [RD-NS-4]. The fare record confirms $6.61 was charged with no surge applied [F7][F8].

Because the rider is the cancelling party, NS-4 is the operative charge rule [F4][F7][RD-NS-4]; the fee stands and no refund is due. The trace marks NS-0 and NS-4 as settled (✓) and the only open element is the safety screen.

The fee can alternatively be tested against NS-1 as the driver-side no-show branch: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point [F6][F1], was first within 200 m at 09:02:40 and accumulated 6 min 30 s inside the radius before cancellation [F2], and stayed stationary 39 m away from 09:03:00 to 09:09:10 [F3]. Even read through NS-1, all three conditions (tap, GPS at pickup, > 3 minutes' wait) are satisfied [F2][F3][F6][RD-NS-1], so the $6.61 fee is not displaced.

The rider's own message at 09:05 asking for "2 more minutes" [F10] does not undo the charge: it shows she was still en route, but it is not consent by the driver to waive the waiting requirement, and the chat is complete and fully timestamped [F12], so it cannot be read as any retraction of the fee [F10][F12][RD-NS-4]. The driver's chat and post-trip statement [F11][F13] are merely corroborative of the wait already measured on GPS [F2][F3].

Amount: no refund is computed because the charge is a published fee validly incurred; with cancellation at 540 s after acceptance [F4] and no surge [F8], the $6.61 stands and the refundable portion is $0.00 [F4][F7][RD-NS-4].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, all three chat messages and the driver's statement [F9][F10][F11][F13] plus the complaint text. Chat #1 is a neutral arrival notice with vehicle description [F9]; chat #2 is the rider asking for two more minutes [F10]; chat #3 states the driver called twice and waited [F11]; the driver's statement repeats the same in neutral terms [F13]. No threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation appears; safety_concern = none [F9][F10][F11][F13][RD-SAFE-1].

Finally, the profile facts for both parties [F17][F18] do not decide the case: the rider's 3 prior disputes with 0 upheld [F17] and the driver's clean record [F18] are irrelevant to whether the charged fee is valid, and neither supports an account flag here — the driver's conduct shows no abuse of the "I'm Here"/waiting button and there is no repeated route/no-show violation [F17][F18][RD-NS-1][RD-NS-2][RD-RD-6].

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The $6.61 cancellation fee charged on this RydeX trip is a fee the rider disputes as wrongful, and the question is whether it survives NS-1 on the system records.

The driver did satisfy the three NS-1 conditions on the system records: he tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00, GPS placed him 39 m from the pickup both at that moment and throughout, and he remained inside the 200 m radius for 6 min 10 s after the tap (6 min 30 s cumulative before cancellation) — far beyond the 3-minute threshold.
The rider is the cancelling party and cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance, i.e. beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, which is the branch NS-0 sends to NS-4

The rider's own message at 09:05 said only "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" (F10), while the driver had already announced his arrival at 09:03 (F9); the chat is fully timestamped and does not retract the fee or show any agreement by the driver to waive the waiting requirement.

The only remaining statutory escape in NS-4 would be a rule that a driver arriving late frees the rider to cancel free of charge, but Ryde publishes no such rule (NS-8 is informational only and is not cited); F5 shows the platform recorded arrival at 09:02:40, only 2 min 30 s after acceptance, so no such argument is available on these facts.

weaknesses: The strongest rider-side point is that the driver himself waited longer than the policy requires and the rider was visibly on the way: F10 ("Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" at 09:05) shows the rider was actively complying and not absconding, which a human reviewer could read as a reason for a discretionary waiver under NS-7; but NS-1 is satisfied on F1/F2/F3/F6, so NS-7's 30-day voucher review is the rider's only route, not a Rules-based win.

F11 and F13 (driver: "Called you twice, no answer. Waited 5 min already" / "waited more than 6 minutes") are driver statements; they do not help the rider because F2/F3/F6 independently corroborate the waiting time on GPS, so the system records beat any attempt to characterise the wait as short.

The rider's profile (F17: 3 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) invites the argument that the rider is a repeat fee-disputer; it cannot decide the case, but it weakens the equitable case for a discretionary waiver and could invite a flag_account request against the rider.

The rider was inside the 200 m zone only in the sense of being proximate in the building; the rider never boarded within 6 min 30 s of the driver's arrival, so any claim built on 'the driver was not really there' is contradicted by F1 (39 m) and F6 ("I'm Here" tapped 39 m away).

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup point, so the arrival prerequisite for a rider no-show cancellation is satisfied (F6, F1).
The driver was inside the 200 m pickup radius from 09:02:40 and stayed there 6 min 30 s before the rider cancelled — far beyond the required 3 minutes (F2, F5).
The driver then sat stationary 39 m from the pickup point from 09:03:00 until cancellation at 09:09:10, i.e. 6 min 10 s of waiting at the stand (F3, F6).

The rider's own message at 09:05 asked for two more minutes, which she did not honour: cancellation came at 09:09:10, more than 3 minutes after her own promised time and after the driver had already messaged her twice (F10, F11, F4).
The trip was an on-demand RydeX booking and the rider cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance, i.e. well outside the 3-minute free-cancellation window, so the $6.61 fee is chargeable (F4, F8).
The driver's account (4.4 years, rating 4.9, 700 trips in 90 days, zero disputes upheld) is consistent with a genuine no-show and offers no basis for a fraud flag (F18).

weaknesses: F3 shows the driver stationary 09:03:00–09:09:10 but the rider's message at 09:05 (F10) shows she was actively communicating and on her way, which the rider will use to argue the fee is harsh even though NS-4 free cancellation is measured strictly from matching, not from the driver's ETA. The rider will also rely on the fact that she never asked to cancel — the fee was triggered by her own cancellation after 3 minutes (F4), a reading the controller may treat sympathetically.

The $6.61 fee is chargeable to the rider, but the driver's only recovery is the $4.50 driver share under NS-1; the remaining $2.11 goes to the platform, and any rider-side voucher issued under NS-7 would not restore the driver's share — a limit on what a driver-side win is actually worth here.

points.response: Conceded on the mechanism: F6 does show the tap at 09:03:00 with F1 placing the driver 39 m away; my case does not deny the tap, it denies that a technical compliance should cost my client $6.61 when she was actively coming down (F10).

F2 and F5 are not in dispute, but they cut the other way for the rider's equity argument: the driver was already on site at 09:02:40 (F5), yet the rider's 09:05 message (F10) shows an ongoing, cooperative rider — this is exactly the fact pattern NS-7's discretionary voucher review exists for, and the strict 3-minute rule in NS-1 does not authorise an automated refusal of that review.

F3 alone cannot establish that the driver's wait was 'unavoidable': the same record shows he was stationary from 09:03:00 to 09:09:10 (F3) while the rider had messaged at 09:05 asking for two minutes (F10), so the driver had notice the rider was en route and could have kept the booking open rather than let the fee attach.

The rider's 09:05 message (F10) is not a no-show admission — it is evidence of the opposite, an actively communicating passenger; F11 is a driver chat message and F13 is a post-trip driver statement, and neither is a system record contradicting that the rider was on her way.

Conceded that F4/F8 place the cancellation 9 min 0 s after acceptance with no surge, so NS-4 charges the fee; the rider's remedy on these undisputed facts is the NS-7 30-day voucher review rather than a contra-NS-4 refund, and I ask the court to route it there.

I do not seek any fraud flag against this driver and accept F18 shows a long clean record; equally, my client's own profile (F17: 0 of 3 disputes upheld) must not be used to prejudge this fee dispute, since profile facts can never decide a case.
Conceded as a framing point only: the dispute does turn on NS-1, and on these records NS-1 is fully made out, so the fee survives and the rider's request for a refund fails (F4, F7).

Agreed and adopted: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while 39 m from the pickup and remained within 200 m for 6 min 10 s after the tap, so all three NS-1 conditions are satisfied (F1, F2, F3, F6).
Agreed: the rider cancelled at 09:09:10, 9 min 0 s after acceptance, so the flat 3-minute free-cancellation rule in NS-4 does not apply and the $6.61 fee stands (F4, F7).

Adopted, and the rider's message at 09:05 asking for two more minutes (F10) is not a retraction of the fee or a waiver by the driver; the rider's own notice that she needed until about 09:07 was already exceeded when she cancelled at 09:09:10 (F4, F10, F12).
Adopted: with platform-recorded arrival at 09:02:40, only 2 min 30 s after acceptance, no driver-lateness argument exists, and Ryde publishes no such free-cancellation rule (F5, F4).
